title: Brazilian court hands player suspension in line with injured opponent’s recovery time
content:
Internacional defender Victor Gabriel has been suspended for the time it will take for Cruzeiro forward Gabriel Pec to recover from a serious injury, a Brazil sports court has ruled.

Pec, 25, suffered a fractured tibia in his left leg on his Cruzeiro debut following a tackle from Gabriel, 22, during the Brazilian Serie A fixture on July 23. The injury required surgery.

The Internacional defender was shown a red card for the challenge, and Brazil’s Superior Court of Sports Justice (STJD) ruled that his ban from playing should be extended until Pec returns to training. The suspension is capped at 180 days.

Gabriel’s challenge 13 minutes into the second half of the fixture at the Estadio Beira-Rio left Pec with a cut on his left leg, and after scans revealed the extent of the injury, charges against Gabriel were filed to the STJD based on the “violence of the play and the severity of the injury”.

It was argued that the challenge was “disproportionate and reckless”, and fell under article 254, 3 of the Brazilian Code of Sports Justice (CBJD), which states that if an athlete is unable to compete due to “serious violent play” then the individual responsible may remain banned until the injured party returns to training, up to a maximum period of 180 days.

Gabriel was in attendance at the STJD’s committee hearing and said he regretted what happened, had apologised to Pec, and had not intended to cause him harm.

“I had the feeling that I would get to the ball first, and I did,” he said. “Since the field was quite slippery and wet, I ended up hitting the ball and then I didn’t have time to pull my leg back, and that’s how this somewhat harder tackle happened, but without any intention of causing harm to my fellow professional or any malice.”

Internacional’s lawyers (Cravo, Pastl e Balbuena Advogados Associados) presented what was claimed to be VAR audio as part of its defence. When questioned regarding its authenticity, they asked it be withdrawn because they could not prove its credibility, and later admitted to and apologised for using an audio recording circulating on social media as evidence.

“Both the law firm and Inter emphasise that they never intended to act in bad faith in any way within the context of the proceedings in question,” a club statement read. “There was, however, a recognised error in the collection and use of the content presented in the player’s defence, which was immediately acknowledged through an express request to remove the audio from the case file.

“The firm, with extensive experience in the field of Sports Law, acknowledges the error and intends to further improve its methods for future trials.”

Pec joined Cruzeiro from LA Galaxy on July 7, returning to Brazil after two years in Major League Soccer.
